questions.q: What does REPLACE(string, findThis, replaceWithThis) match on?
options: The text itself — every occurrence of findThis, wherever it appears
A fixed position in the string
Only the first character of the string
The string's total length
questions.explain: REPLACE has no concept of position — it swaps every occurrence of matching text, regardless of where it falls.

questions.q: What does STUFF(string, start, length, replaceWith) operate on?
options: A position and length, regardless of what characters are actually there
Matching text, exactly like REPLACE
Only numeric values
The entire string, ignoring the start and length arguments
questions.explain: STUFF deletes a specific number of characters starting at a specific position and inserts new text there — content-agnostic.

questions.q: Why can't REPLACE be used to mask phone number digits that vary per row?
options: REPLACE requires knowing the exact text to find, which is impossible when the digits differ on every row
REPLACE only works on numeric columns
REPLACE can only replace one character at a time
REPLACE actually works fine for this — STUFF offers no advantage
questions.explain: This is exactly the scenario STUFF solves — it only needs a position, not knowledge of the actual content.

Every occurrence of the text '5' in the phone number
The first 5 characters of the phone number
Nothing — this is invalid syntax
questions.explain: STUFF's start/length arguments define the position window to replace, independent of content.

questions.q: What is the core distinction between REPLACE and STUFF?
options: REPLACE matches by content wherever it occurs; STUFF replaces by position regardless of content
REPLACE only works on CHAR columns; STUFF only works on VARCHAR
STUFF can only be used with numbers, REPLACE only with text
There is no meaningful difference between them
questions.explain: This content-vs-position distinction determines which function fits a given problem.
